scope: Read-only primary-source review for the PS4/PS5 host controls. No console connection or payload execution.

release.verification: Metadata read from GitHub release API; this research did not download or execute the asset. Check local archive inventory separately.

service.nativeUIRequired: Version 0.6.3 restricts browser CORS and writes to its own exact HTTP origin. An external website cannot directly operate this API with browser fetch.
service.readIdentity: GET /version returns text; GET /getip returns text.
service.transport: HTTP on TCP 8084; manager sends payloads to its console ELF loader on TCP 9021.
originRules: Mutation routes require POST; GET receives HTTP 405.
If Origin exists it must equal http:// plus Host, including port; Referer is checked when Origin is absent.
Requests without Origin and Referer may use X-PLDMGR-Request: 1. This is intended for native nonbrowser clients, not a bypass available to external website JavaScript.
Access-Control-Allow-Origin is returned only for the exact same origin; external GET response bodies are also unavailable to browser fetch.
Host matching is CSRF protection, not authentication.
service.recommendedIntegration: Open native manager deep links. A paired native local sender could proxy verified operations later, but external-page no-cors fetch is not a usable management API.

nativeLinks.label: Import known USB payload
nativeLinks.note: Requires an actual discovered path; route without a path falls back to storage.

unsupportedDeepLinkAssumptions: mode=manage and mode=favorites are history states, but the initial navigation effect deletes mode/modal before seeding history. Do not promise that an external manage-mode deep link opens edit mode. Open the dashboard, then use Manage in the native app.
No general console file-manager route is supplied by this project. Use the existing ezRemote native client for arbitrary filesystem management.

storage.selectionRule: Use actual slot keys supplied by /list_payloads. Do not synthesize slot keys from display names or version filenames. USB entries use their discovered console paths.

listResponse.self: Manager running and pending version metadata
listResponse.items: Array with slot, path, kind and filename; repository entries include id, source_url, name, version and checksum metadata.
listResponse.usb: Array of discovered USB payload paths

storage.scanning: Lists internal managed slots, scans /mnt/usb0/pldmgr through /mnt/usb7/pldmgr, and additionally scans only the USB roots for .elf/.bin when SCAN_USB_PAYLOADS is enabled.

autoload.exampleIsIllustrative: Replace example slot keys with actual installed items. Saving does not run the sequence immediately.
autoload.fileFormat: One slot key or delay entry per line, preserving list order.
autoload.delayEntry: !N waits N milliseconds between entries; accepted range is 0 through 3600000.
autoload.startupDelay: AUTOLOAD_DELAY is an integer in seconds, accepted range 0 through 3600; default 5.
autoload.booleans: Settings JSON uses real JSON booleans; on-disk settings use KEY=0 or KEY=1.
autoload.returnAfterSuccess: AUTOLOAD_RETURN_TO_DASHBOARD defaults false; the native UI may return after about three seconds only when every payload succeeded.
autoload.processBoundary: Manager autoload starts when the manager is launched. This is separate from an exploit/autoloader's own autoload.txt.
autoload.abort: POST /abort stops the current autoload sequence.
autoload.clearStatus: POST /autoload_clear resets execution status; it does not remove configured autoload entries.
autoload.status: GET /autoload_status supplies state, remaining, total, done, current, successful, failed, skipped and outcomes. An authorized native GET marks the frontend ready, so it is not entirely passive.
autoload.safeUI: Autoload editor supports add, remove, up/down order, explicit delay entries and enable/disable with serial autosave. Never claim a save succeeded before the server acknowledgement.

settings.partialUpdates: POST /set_config accepts an object containing only changed keys and preserves unrelated settings.
settings.favorites: FAVORITES accepts CSV or an array of strings; use installed slot keys.

Inspect upload filename conflicts before uploading

Run installed or USB payload; this is execution and is outside this task's read-only verification

Remove source by actual current index

managementEndpoints.body: Sources JSON used by native Manage Sources view

repositoryFormat.wrapper: Object with name and payloads array, or bare array; prefer wrapper.
repositoryFormat.checksum: SHA-256 as 64 hex characters; provide known hashes. Binary/catalog fetching happens in console daemon, so browser CORS is not needed for those downloads.
repositoryFormat.pinning: Only include PS5-supported payloads and preserve firmware/feature compatibility. A catalogue download installs a file; a separate native action runs it.

bootstrap.managerReadme: Use the manager as the only payload in the chosen compatible autoloader's own sequence when manager-controlled ordering is desired.
bootstrap.currentY2JB: Current upstream Y2JB defaults to the manager if no autoload.txt exists. Manual files are in USB-root/ps5_autoloader or /data/ps5_autoloader, with USB taking priority. Its sequence and the manager's /data/pldmgr/autoload.txt are distinct.
bootstrap.loopbackLoader: Current Y2JB's bundled elfldr accepts localhost only by default; desktop TCP 9021 sending can fail even when manager operations work. Do not silently replace it or imply every ELF loader accepts remote connections.
bootstrap.initial9020Versus9021: The upstream elfldr README documents sending elfldr-ps5.elf to an exploit's initial basic ELF loader on TCP 9020. Once elfldr is running it accepts ordinary payloads on TCP 9021. Use the actual chosen exploit's stage and firmware; do not assume every entry point starts the same port.
bootstrap.compatibility: Keep the host's existing firmware/entry-point pins; this research does not extend them.

ps4.managerCompatibilityEvidence: The itsPLK manager is PS5-native; no source confirms it as a PS4 manager.
ps4.nativeManager: GoldHEN PayLoader LaunchPad and AutoRun Queue
workflow: Use the PS4 file manager/downloader or GoldHEN FTP to save a compatible BIN/ELF in /data/payloads/.
Open GoldHEN, Utilities, PayLoader LaunchPad on the console.
Select a payload to run once; Square adds it to AutoRun Queue.
Review enabled entries in AutoRun Queue; disable an older entry before adding a new version.
ps4.pathCaution: Control4Free documents /data/payloads/ for copying and the exact /user/data/payloads/ registration above. This review does not establish a universal alias rule between these paths; use the native Queue UI and actual generated entry.
ps4.queueExampleLimit: The exact example is documented by Control4Free's author. GoldHEN's internal binary implementation is not public, so generic order/delay semantics and complete INI preservation are not confirmed. Prefer native Queue UI over external blind rewrites.
ps4.payloadSender: GoldHEN PayLoader/BinLoader TCP 9090 when enabled; this is raw payload transport, not HTTP file management.
ps4.webManagementAPI: No GoldHEN HTTP queue API or native browser deep link confirmed. Do not show a fake http://IP:9090 manager or route PS4 to PS5 port 8084.
ps4.fallback: Provide local Download and Save controls, a valid ezRemote native file-manager link, and honest console steps for GoldHEN LaunchPad/AutoRun. Separate older firmware/GoldHEN builds that lack this feature.

verificationLimits: No physical PS4 or PS5 connected.
No payload downloaded, sent, loaded, installed or executed by this research.
No local F: archive records were changed.
No source/catalogue files were edited; only this evidence document was added.
Source-confirmed behavior is not evidence of hardware execution success.
